text:
The score says 5-2, but the game was tied at two until late in the second period, and the Rangers were already winning the chances by then. Over the first period the two teams were nearly level (1.22 expected goals for NYI, 1.14 for NYR). From there the Rangers pulled away. They outchanced the Islanders 1.68 to 0.8 in the second and 2.43 to 0.23 in the third, and in simulated replays of every shot they win this game 75 percent of the time.

Alexis Lafrenière carried it. He scored three times and added an assist, with 1.5 expected goals on his own shots, so the output matched the looks he got. His first came 25 seconds into the second period, a snap shot that made it 2-0. NYI answered fast: Bo Horvat scored on the power play at 2:56, and Calum Ritchie tied it at 4:52. Oliver Bjorkstrand restored the lead on a power play at 17:07 of the second, his second goal of the night.

The final margin came from two goals 32 seconds apart in the closing minutes. Lafrenière scored at 18:22 and again at 18:54, with scoring chances of 76 and 69 percent, shots the Islanders could not realistically stop. Semyon Varlamov was not the problem, finishing 0.8 goals better than expected on 22 shots against. New York held a 56-47 edge in shot attempts and a 27-18 edge in hits, and took the puck away six times to the Islanders' two. Mika Zibanejad had two assists and Adam Fox and Vladislav Gavrikov drove play from the back end.
